title: Weather Balloons
text: The weather service is short of staff and some offices have stopped launching weather balloons. Slides are provided. Nobody on them is gold.

options.label: Read every slide
options.result: You learned what a weather balloon does. You asked if it could carry a banner.

ignore.text: Forecasters guessed the sky. The sky declined to confirm.

inspiredBy: Reports in 2025 of weather service offices cutting balloon launches amid staff losses.

title: Climate Assessment
text: Scientists have a national climate report, and a long argument about whether the website hosting it should exist. Sit through the chapters.

options.label: Sit through the chapters
options.result: Chapter 9 was about coastlines. You asked whether yours could be rebranded.

ignore.text: The report was published anyway, by people with no one to stop them.

inspiredBy: 2025 removal of the National Climate Assessment website and dismissal of its authors.

title: Disaster Season Review
text: A council wants to review whether disaster response should shift to the states. The review has 140 pages and an appendix about forms.

options.label: Review the forms
options.result: You approved a plan that ensures every form has a place to sit.

ignore.text: The review was never signed. The next storm filed its own.

inspiredBy: 2025 FEMA review council debating shifting disaster response to the states.

title: Moon Schedule
text: Engineers walk you through the Artemis schedule: another delay, a heat shield, a revised landing date. You asked for a landing in your honor.

options.label: Hear out the engineers
options.result: The Moon is still on track for eventually. Your name is not on the lander.

ignore.text: The launch window closed while you picked a font for the crew patch.

inspiredBy: 2025 and 2026 Artemis program delays and schedule revisions.

title: AI Rules Patchwork
text: Lawyers brief you on the clash between state AI laws and a single national rulebook. One slide is a map of states in angry colors.

options.label: Sit through the map
options.result: You now understand preemption. You still prefer the word "winning."

ignore.text: Fifty states wrote fifty AI laws. A lawyer cried in a hallway.

inspiredBy: Late 2025 executive order seeking to override state AI regulations.

title: Golden Dome Briefing
text: Generals present the missile shield: layers, sensors, a price tag with a surprising number of zeroes. You ask whether the dome is actually gold.

options.label: Hear the cost estimates
options.result: The dome is not gold. The estimate is, in a way.

ignore.text: The shield got designed by committee. The committee has been issued an umbrella.

inspiredBy: 2025 Golden Dome missile defense plan and its cost estimates.

title: Advisory Panel Minutes
text: The vaccine advisory panel has issued six hours of minutes. Doctors on both sides would like a senior official to remember the minutes exist.

options.label: Read all six hours
options.result: You learned how to say "immunization schedule" without pausing.

ignore.text: The minutes went unread. The footnotes held a grudge.

inspiredBy: 2025 reconstitution of the CDC vaccine advisory committee and its contested meetings.

title: Reactor Licensing
text: Officials want sign-off on faster approvals for small nuclear reactors. They show a diagram that is not shaped like a ballroom.

options.label: Review the licensing plan
options.result: You approved a streamlined process and asked if one could be built in the Rose Garden. No.

ignore.text: The licensing backlog stayed long. The reactors stayed theoretical.

inspiredBy: 2025 executive orders to speed up nuclear reactor approvals.

title: Offshore Windmills
text: An energy adviser says halting a half-built offshore wind farm will cost billions and invite a lawsuit. The windmills block your view of nothing.

options.label: Let the lawyers advise
options.result: The lawyers won. The windmills turned, unforgiven.

options.label: Order the turbines stopped
options.result: The turbines froze mid-spin, like a photo of a windmill that someone hates.

ignore.text: The wind farm sat half-finished. Seagulls moved in.

inspiredBy: 2025 stop-work orders and pauses on offshore wind projects, with court challenges.

title: Coal Plant Order
text: A utility wants to retire a coal plant on schedule. Engineers say the grid has enough power. An aide holds out a "keep it open" order.

options.label: Let it retire
options.result: The plant retired with a small ceremony and a lot of relief on the grid.

options.label: Order it kept open
options.result: Coal lives. The plant manager sent flowers and a hefty repair bill.

ignore.text: The plant is in limbo and the old turbine is making noises.

inspiredBy: 2025 emergency orders keeping coal plants open past retirement dates.

title: Showerhead Question
text: An aide says the old water-saving rules are law, and a law is a law. You recall a shower that dribbled in a way that felt personal.

options.label: Study the law
options.result: The law stands. Your hair, as ever, is not ruled by water pressure.

options.label: Demand more water pressure
options.result: The shower roared like a waterfall. The plumbing bill was a small flood.

ignore.text: The rule remains in force. You took a cold shower anyway.

inspiredBy: 2025 push to roll back water-saving appliance and showerhead standards.

title: Mars Deadline
text: A space adviser says Mars landings are decades off and the Moon needs finishing first. A tech CEO says Mars by next spring. He means it, somehow.

options.label: Fund the Moon plan first
options.result: The Moon plan advanced slowly. Mars grew a little more patient.

options.label: Announce Mars by next spring
options.result: The calendar accepts your date. Rockets do not read calendars.

ignore.text: The space plan was left floating. Nobody could agree on where.

inspiredBy: 2025 debates over prioritizing Mars versus the Moon in NASA plans.

title: Chip Export Deal
text: A trade adviser proposes a deal letting an AI chip maker sell a cut-down chip abroad, with a cut to the Treasury. Security staff keep clearing their throats.

options.label: Take the security advice
options.result: The chips stayed home. The chip maker sent a stern memo.

options.label: Cut the deal, take a cut
options.result: The Treasury got a cut. Your security people got migraines.

ignore.text: The licensing question sat unanswered. The chips found their own route.

inspiredBy: 2025 deal letting Nvidia sell AI chips to China in exchange for a revenue share.

title: Neutral AI Order
text: An adviser says government AI systems should be tested for accuracy, not ideology. A draft order calls an assistant "too polite to you."

options.label: Require accuracy tests
options.result: The tests were dull and fair. The chatbot remained unreasonably courteous.

options.label: Order the AI to call you great
options.result: The AI complied with a 40-paragraph tribute. Auditors noticed.

ignore.text: The AI guidance stayed vague. Every vendor wrote its own.

inspiredBy: 2025 AI Action Plan and order on "woke AI" in federal procurement.

title: Electric Car Credit
text: Aides say ending the electric car tax credit will hit sales and a few factories. A tycoon at the other end of the supply chain would like a word.

options.label: Phase it out gently
options.result: The phase-out was gradual. The factories adjusted their sighs.

options.label: End it immediately
options.result: The credit died on Friday. The car companies held a quiet vigil.

ignore.text: The credit expired by default and the showrooms noticed.

inspiredBy: 2025 repeal of electric vehicle tax credits.

title: Name The Shield
text: The missile shield needs a name for the press release. "Golden Dome" is already taken. Naming it after yourself requires a form.

options.label: Keep the working title
options.result: The shield is called what it was called. Engineers cheered.

options.label: Rename it after yourself
options.result: The brass plaque is already on order. The shield has not been designed.

ignore.text: The shield was announced without a name. The press picked one.

inspiredBy: 2025 Golden Dome announcement and its naming.

title: Space Shuttle Move
text: Aides propose moving a retired space shuttle from one museum to another city. The museum and the lawyers object. The shuttle has no opinion.

options.label: Leave the shuttle alone
options.result: The shuttle stayed. It still looks great, parked.

options.label: Sign the shuttle order
options.result: The shuttle was moved. A crane, a state, and an angry senator are pending.

ignore.text: The shuttle stayed in limbo. A committee now owns the parking.

inspiredBy: 2025 proposal to relocate a retired space shuttle in a budget bill.

title: Health Body Exit
text: Doctors warn that leaving the global health organization will cut off disease data. Aides say the dues are steep and the building is far away.

options.label: Keep the data link
options.result: The data kept flowing. The dues were tolerated, with grumbling.

options.label: Walk out, make a speech
options.result: You walked out. The data turned off, like an unpaid utility.

ignore.text: The paperwork sat in limbo. Epidemiologists made their own links.

inspiredBy: 2025 order to withdraw the US from the World Health Organization.

title: Drug Price Site
text: Pharma aides propose a government site for cheaper medicine. Doctors say to include clear safety information. The site name is already yours.

options.label: Add the safety information
options.result: The site shows dosages and warnings. It feels like a pharmacy, not a billboard.

options.label: Launch it with your face
options.result: The site launched with a large portrait. The pills are not in the photo.

ignore.text: The site is half-built. A banner reads "coming soon, and great."

inspiredBy: 2025 announcement of a TrumpRx drug price website.

title: Straw Question
text: A reporter asks about your ban on paper straws. She says they dissolve in the drink, and that it is a big issue in your drink.

options.label: Say you will review it
options.result: You reviewed it. Soup was found to be a different issue.

options.label: Call paper straws a disaster
options.result: The line plays well. The plastic straw lobby sends a gift basket.

ignore.text: The straw question went unanswered. Sippy cups were rumored.

inspiredBy: 2025 executive order promoting plastic straws over paper straws.

title: Physical Results
text: A reporter asks about your annual physical and the cognitive test. The doctor wants a calm, accurate summary, not a victory lap.

options.label: Let the doctor speak
options.result: The doctor read the results. They were fine. It lasted four minutes.

options.label: Announce a perfect score
options.result: You said "perfect" eleven times. The test is a short screening.

ignore.text: No one briefed the press. Everyone made up their own diagnosis.

inspiredBy: April 2025 annual physical and the reported cognitive screening test score.

title: The Eclipse
text: An eclipse is passing over Washington. Scientists have handed out special glasses and one very clear instruction.

options.label: Wear the glasses
options.result: You wore the glasses like everybody else. In the photos you are indistinguishable from an aide.

options.label: Look straight at it
options.result: You stared it down. The sun blinked first, you said. An optometrist has asked for a word.

ignore.text: You missed the eclipse. The photo of the empty balcony ran on every front page.

inspiredBy: The 2017 solar eclipse viewed from the White House balcony.

title: Tech Dinner Toast
text: A state dinner with tech CEOs begins. Each wants a regulation lifted. Aides suggest a short toast. You prefer a long one that features you.

options.label: Keep the toast short
options.result: The toast was short. Dessert came in time to be happy.

options.label: Ask who is richest
options.result: You asked who invested the most. Phone cameras came out in unison.

ignore.text: The dinner had no toast. The CEOs toasted each other.

inspiredBy: September 2025 White House dinner with major tech CEOs.

title: Science Mission Event
text: At an event for a new AI science program, a reporter asks how it will work. The scientists would like to answer. They stand behind you.

options.label: Hand the mic to scientists
options.result: A scientist explained it in plain words. You nodded as if you wrote it.

options.label: Say it will be tremendous
options.result: You said "tremendous" four times. The scientists stared at their shoes.

ignore.text: The event ended with no explanation. The scientists went to lunch.

inspiredBy: Late 2025 executive order launching the Genesis Mission for AI-driven science.

title: Climate Remarks
text: At an international gathering, you are about to speak on climate. Scientists want you to respect the data. Your speechwriter has a different opinion.

options.label: Read the data fairly
options.result: The speech cited real data. Several diplomats were pleased and confused.

options.label: Call it a con job
options.result: The hall gasped. You counted it as applause.

ignore.text: The speech was never written. You ad-libbed the weather.

inspiredBy: September 2025 UN speech calling climate change a "con job."

title: Doctor On The Line
text: A doctor calls about the scan you had. Everything looks normal and she wants to explain in detail. You want to tell her it was "amazing."

options.label: Listen to the full report
options.result: It was an ordinary scan. The doctor was relieved that you listened.

options.label: Announce it was perfect
options.result: You told the press it was "perfect," and the doctor winced politely.

ignore.text: No one returned the doctor's call. The scan sits in a drawer.

inspiredBy: October 2025 reports of a routine MRI at Walter Reed and the White House statements about it.

title: NASA Chief Calls
text: The NASA chief calls about the budget and a nomination that was pulled and then restored. He asks only for a plain answer.

options.label: Give a clear answer
options.result: You answered clearly. The call lasted six minutes, which is a record.

options.label: Ask about a Moon statue
options.result: You asked about a gold statue on the Moon. The line went silent.

ignore.text: The call went to voicemail. The mission chose its own budget.

inspiredBy: 2025 nomination, withdrawal and renomination of the NASA administrator.

title: Name That Comet
text: Astronomers have spotted a visitor from another star system. By convention it is named after the telescope that found it.

options.label: Congratulate the astronomers
options.result: You congratulated a telescope. It did not congratulate you back.

options.label: Sign an order naming it after you
options.result: The comet bears your name on all federal documents. It is leaving the solar system as fast as it can.

ignore.text: The comet passed unremarked. Several agencies issued rival names for it.

inspiredBy: The interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, discovered in July 2025.

title: Power Grid Call
text: A grid operator calls: data centers are using more power than the grid can provide. She asks for a plan that adds actual generation.

options.label: Back a real power plan
options.result: The plan added power, and a cable. The call was dull.

options.label: Say AI will invent more power
options.result: You said AI will think of something. The operator took notes, sadly.

ignore.text: The call went unreturned. Servers and lamps argued over the outlets.

inspiredBy: 2025 concerns about data center electricity demand straining the grid.

title: Vaccine Lab Call
text: A lab director calls: federal funding for vaccine technology projects was canceled, and she wants to keep a few trials going. She asks for five minutes.

options.label: Keep the trials funded
options.result: The trials survived. She thanked you and then thanked the lab techs.

options.label: Say you prefer something else
options.result: You said you have a better idea. It had no name yet.

ignore.text: The lab never heard back. The freezer was left with a sticky note.

inspiredBy: August 2025 cancellation of federal mRNA vaccine research contracts.
